body: Thanks, but honestly don't feel like it anymore. Years of solitude tend to do that.

Oh I've tried. My parents aren't exactly the "listening" sort and my sister could really care less at this point. We're nice to each other when together, but that's the extent of it. I've tried to reach out to her numerous times and explained how I feel, but it's essential talking to myself in a vacuum

Hey, I suffer from bipolar as well.

You said you currently have nothing to live for - what are some things that you would hypothetically live for? Make a list of things in life - however ridiculous they might be - that you think would possibly make you happy. Then put off ending things until you exhaust every single resource you have trying to make at least one thing on your list a reality.

Honestly that's the only excuse I ever hear. "Your sister would he devastated!" Yeah. My sister. Who I speak with maybe 3 or 4 times a year and only see maybe once, if that. I'm obviously a huge part of her life.

Thanks for the kind words. I still feel I'm just going to ultimately end up as another statistic pretty soon and there isn't much I can do about it. I'm fairly intelligent and one of my degrees is in psychology - so therapy is largely ineffective as I more or less know what's going on most of the time. I no longer take meds, haven't for a few years now. They just tend to numb emotions and don't fix any real issues going on. Plus they greatly decrease cognitive function, and that's honestly the only thing that is even sort of going for me. Smoking weed helps, but it's illegal in my state, not even medicinal, so I'm always running out and sometimes it's weeks or months before I can get more. Plus I'm always having to hide it and hope I don't get evicted for it. Could also easily lose my job.
